hook_text: Three ways to move a triangle on a grid, three rules, and one quick check that catches every mix-up.
clip_script: Triangle ABC sits on a grid with A at 1 semicolon 2. Move one: the mirror. Reflect in the x-axis and the axis keeps its own number: x stays 1, y flips to negative 2. Reflect in the slanted line y equals x and the numbers just swap: 2 semicolon 1. Move two: the slide. 3 left and 2 down means subtract 3 and subtract 2: A lands on negative 2 semicolon 0. Move three: the turn. A quarter turn anticlockwise about the origin swaps the numbers and makes the first one negative: negative 2 semicolon 1. Clockwise makes the second one negative instead: 2 semicolon negative 1. Cannot remember which? Check the quadrant. A starts top right; a quarter turn anticlockwise must land it top left, where x is negative. Mirror, slide, turn, and check the quadrant.
visual_style: A yellow triangle on a clean grid; a blue mirror image flips below the x-axis; a dashed diagonal mirror swaps it; an orange copy slides left and down; a purple copy swings a quarter turn with a curved arrow, and the quadrant lights up.
pacing: Brisk moves, each rule stated once, a pause on the quadrant check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for every rule, rotations about any point, and the five common errors.
